questions.question: The Kirchenbauer et al. (2023) text watermarking mechanism works by:
options: Appending a hidden signature token to every generated sequence
Hashing the previous K tokens to partition the vocabulary into green and red sets, then biasing sampling toward green tokens at each step — detectable by the green-token z-score
Training the model to embed specific Unicode characters at fixed positions in its output
Encoding a binary watermark in the model's logit distribution that is recoverable by the model owner
questions.explanation: The Kirchenbauer mechanism: at each decoding step, hash the previous K tokens to produce a pseudorandom green/red vocabulary split. Add delta to green logit scores. The watermarked text contains more green tokens than chance, detectable via z-score. The key is the vocabulary partition function — without it, detection is impossible.

questions.question: Stable Signature (Fernandez et al., ICCV 2023) embeds an image watermark by:
options: Adding invisible pixel-level noise to the generated image
Fine-tuning the latent diffusion decoder so every output contains a fixed binary message recoverable by a neural decoder
Encoding the model's digital signature in the image's EXIF metadata
Inserting a fixed spatial frequency pattern that survives JPEG compression
questions.explanation: Stable Signature fine-tunes the latent diffusion decoder — the component that converts latent representations to images — so it always embeds a fixed binary message. Detection requires a trained neural decoder. At 10% cropping, detection exceeded 90% accuracy at FPR < 1e-6. The decoder is the embedding surface, not the pixel space.

questions.question: C2PA is complementary to watermarking rather than redundant. What does C2PA provide that watermarks cannot?
options: C2PA embeds provenance information that survives aggressive image manipulation
C2PA provides a rich, cryptographically signed provenance chain (who created, when, what transformations) that carries more information than the few bits a watermark can embed
C2PA detection works without access to the original model
C2PA is mandatory under EU AI Act while watermarks are optional
questions.explanation: Watermarks persist through transcoding but carry minimal information (essentially: was this AI-generated?). C2PA metadata carries a full provenance chain — creator identity, timestamps, transformation history — but can be stripped. They are complementary: watermarks for persistence, C2PA for rich provenance detail.

questions.question: The 2024 'Stable Signature is Unstable' result demonstrated what vulnerability?
options: The watermark decoder can be reverse-engineered from the public model checkpoint
Fine-tuning the decoder removes the watermark while preserving image quality — adversarial post-generation fine-tuning of the decoder is cheap and effective
High-compression JPEG saves destroy the watermark signal
The watermark is detectable by standard image forensics tools, allowing attackers to avoid watermarked outputs
questions.explanation: 'Stable Signature is Unstable' (arXiv:2405.07145, May 2024) showed that fine-tuning the decoder — the same component that embeds the watermark — removes the watermark while maintaining image quality. The attack is cheap and accessible to anyone who can fine-tune a diffusion decoder.

questions.question: SynthID-text detection is not robust to which common transformation?
options: Changing the font or visual presentation of the text
Paraphrasing — rewriting the text destroys the green-token signal because the vocabulary partition depends on the specific tokens generated
Translating the text to another language and back
Removing punctuation and formatting from the text
questions.explanation: Text watermarks based on token-level green/red partitioning are not robust to paraphrase: when the text is rewritten with different words, the hash-derived vocabulary partitions no longer apply to the new tokens, destroying the statistical signal. Image watermarks can survive cropping because pixel-level features are retained; token watermarks cannot survive semantic-preserving rewording.

questions.question: What does it mean that 'no SynthID signal' is NOT proof of authenticity in a deployment?
options: SynthID detection has too high a false-positive rate to be reliable
SynthID only marks outputs from SynthID-enabled models — a human-created document and an AI document from a non-SynthID model both lack the signal, so absence of watermark cannot distinguish them
SynthID watermarks can be removed without detection, so attackers always remove them before publishing
The SynthID z-score threshold is set too high, causing many genuine watermarks to be missed
questions.explanation: SynthID embeds a signal only in outputs from models that have SynthID enabled. A human-authored document, an AI document from a model without SynthID, and a paraphrased SynthID-watermarked document all lack the signal. 'No watermark detected' cannot distinguish these cases — it is evidence about provenance only when combined with knowledge of what models were potentially used.
